routeDescriptionClues.description: The route begins in/near Guovdageaidnu/Kautokeino, passes the Buletjávri/Arctic Motell side of town, then follows a road/path mix into wet birch, bog and reindeer-herding terrain toward Čunovuohppi. Several recent hikers describe the Kautokeino approach as muddy, brushy and sometimes bypassed by road.

Reisa describes access from Kautokeino via route 93/route 6 to Cunovuohppi and notes that winter road clearing is only as far as Cunovuohppi. It also cautions that many roads/tracks in the area are used for reindeer husbandry and may not lead where hikers intend.

campingAndFire.summary: This section transitions between the closed/legacy Čunovuohppi endpoint, remote wet plateau/birch/reindeer terrain, and Kautokeino town services. No verified route-side shelter, hut, public toilet, fireplace or potable-water point was found between Čunovuohppi and Kautokeino.
campingNotes: FeFo/allemannsrett outfield camping principles likely apply away from settlement/private cabins, roads and reindeer infrastructure: camp carefully, more than 150 m from inhabited houses/cabins, and do not stay more than two nights in the same place without landowner permission.
Buletjávri camp site is OSM/Wikivoyage-supported but lacks official facility details; keep pending.
Arctic Motell & Kautokeino Camping is a strong town endpoint camping/lodging service, not a route-side wilderness camp.
shelterNotes: No verified open shelter or hut between Čunovuohppi and Kautokeino was found.
Do not treat Madam Bongos as a shelter or lodging service; current evidence points to closed/deleted/no operation.
fireNotes: General Norwegian open-fire ban applies 15 April-15 September in/near forest and outfield unless fire risk is clearly absent.
Avoid fires near private cabins, settlement, reindeer infrastructure and dry vegetation; check municipal and national fire-risk status before use.

rules.fire: General Norwegian open-fire ban applies 15 April-15 September in/near forest and outfield unless fire risk is clearly absent.
rules.dogs: National leash requirement applies 1 April-20 August. No Kautokeino-specific extension was confirmed, but this is active reindeer country and dogs should be under strict control year-round around reindeer/herding activity.
rules.privateRoadAccess: The road to Čunovuohppi fjellstue was downgraded to private road from 2024-07-01. Do not imply guaranteed public vehicle access, parking or active lodging.
rules.snowmobileMotor: Kautokeino snowmobile routes are regulated and open only when marked/declared open by the municipality; normal closure from 5 May with possible changes. Route 16 Hánnojávri-Biedjovággi passes through/near Čunovuohppi/Stuorajávri in snowmobile regulations, but this is seasonal motor-access context, not hiking geometry.
rules.reindeer: Cunovuohppi has documented reindeer migration and winter-pasture sensitivity. Keep distance from herds/herding work, avoid blocking fences/tracks and avoid camping or lingering near herds.
rules.huntingFishing: FeFo hunting/fishing rules apply by area. Kautokeino spring duck-hunting regulation through 2028 includes named waters such as Stuorajávri; early May to early June can overlap local hunting near lakes/water.

safetyHazards: Field reports repeatedly describe the Kautokeino approach as muddy, boggy, brushy and sometimes hard to follow.
Several hikers used or considered road alternatives because of wet/boggy trail conditions near Kautokeino.
Road/private-road and reindeer-herding tracks can be ambiguous; do not assume every track is public or leads to the route.
No verified services at the Čunovuohppi/Madam Bongos endpoint; plan water, shelter and transport conservatively.

conditionReports.observations: Near Kautokeino the route became hard to follow, with birch, bog, marsh, biting insects, intermittent red blazes and knee-deep black bog. Later bypassed the Čunovuohppi/Madam Bongos loop by taking an unmarked higher path to avoid boggy forest. Met Sámi workers on quad bikes checking reindeer/fences.
conditionReports.confidence: high for terrain pattern but stale

conditionReports.title: Vanja Jovanic - Kautokeino to Kilpisjärvi
conditionReports.direction: Kautokeino to Madam Bongos to Reisavannhytta
conditionReports.observations: Chose the road to Madam Bongos after reading warnings about Kautokeino swamps. Madam Bongos was operating then but appeared disorderly; host had little current trail information. After rejoining trail, reports mud, ATV-damaged wet areas, steel matting, mosquitoes and route-finding issues.
conditionReports.confidence: medium-high but stale; service status superseded by 2019/2024/2025 closure evidence

sourceContradictions.details: Reisa overview says 22 km; Reisa poster says 20 km; E1 GPX and OSM E1 parent geometry measure about 19.36 km; OSM child relation 9517537 tags 19.4 km but current members measure only about 17.09 km; field road exits are about 9-12 km.
sourceContradictions.impact: Use official 22 km for source-reported stage metadata, but do not treat it as geometry length. Normalize display policy later.

sourceContradictions.details: OSM relation 9517537 is named Buletjávri-Čunovuohppi and omits the Kautokeino-to-Buletjávri approach. The OSM E1 parent relation or E1 GPX includes the missing approach.
sourceContradictions.impact: Do not use child relation 9517537 alone for section import.

sourceContradictions.details: Reisa still lists Madam Bongos fjellstue as endpoint, but Brønnøysund says the entity was deleted 2019-05-28, UT says the fjellstue is closed, municipal strategy calls Čunovuohppi the former fjellstue, and municipal minutes downgraded the road due no operation.
sourceContradictions.impact: Treat as legacy place/access endpoint, not active lodging/service.

sourceContradictions.details: Reisa names Kautokeino but does not publish a precise terminus. E1/OSM route endpoint is about 180 m from Kartverket town centre and about 0.27 km from Kautokeino rådhus stop.

sourceContradictions.details: Recent field reports describe road walking or road bypasses for the wet Kautokeino approach, while official/E1 geometry preserves a longer marked trail/path stage.

sourceContradictions.details: No active protected-area overlap was verified, but an older government planning decision describes proposed Stuorajávri wetland/nature-reserve sensitivity and reindeer migration/winter-pasture concerns near Čunovuohppi.
sourceContradictions.impact: Use careful sensitivity wording and GIS/Lovdata verification before applying protected-area tags.
